answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before its votes count, then slash that stake when a randomly audited claim is false. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply influence: every account must fund its own bond, and coordinated lies risk losing all of them. The walnut, basalt, and sonnet labels can be assigned to audited test cases, making the challenge set easy to recognize without changing the rule. The attacker pays real capital and audit exposure for each extra identity.
